summary.oneLiner: JD Cables doubled its order book to Rs. 286 Cr. and is aggressively expanding capacity via a new Dankuni facility, with conductor division commissioning in Dec 2025-Jan 2026 to double output by March 2026, while entering EPC to capture forward integration upside and target Rs. 1,000 Cr. order book by FY27-28.

one-line thesis: JD Cables doubled its order book to Rs. 286 Cr. and is aggressively expanding capacity via a new Dankuni facility, with conductor division commissioning in Dec 2025-Jan 2026 to double output by March 2026, while entering EPC to capture forward integration upside and target Rs. 1,000 Cr. order book by FY27-28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +13% YoY to Rs. 121.44 Cr.; EBITDA: +25% YoY to Rs. 19.24 Cr. (margin 15.85% vs 13.62% in FY25); PAT: +16% YoY to Rs. 11.92 Cr. (margin 9.82% vs 8.84% in FY25); Order Book: Rs. 286.21 Cr. (2.36x H1 revenue); Net Debt: Net cash position post-IPO proceeds (Rs. 96 Cr. raised); no one-offs or accounting distortions noted
guidance: Revenue growth: Target Rs. 350-360 Cr. for FY26, Rs. 500-600 Cr. for FY27, Rs. 1,000 Cr. by FY27-28; Margin: EBITDA to remain 15-16%, PAT margins stable; Order inflow: Targeting Rs. 60 Cr. in pending EPC tenders, more to follow; Capex/Commissioning: Rs. 6-7 Cr. for cable division in H2FY26, total capex ~Rs. 160-170 Cr. to reach Rs. 1,000 Cr. order book
order book & pipeline: Rs. 286.21 Cr. as of Sep 30, 2025; 12-18 month execution horizon; Rs. 60 Cr. in pending EPC tenders awaiting results
segment / subsidiary detail: Cables: 70-80% of revenue; Conductors: growing segment; EPC: new division, targeting 150-200 Cr. revenue in FY27; HTLS, MVCC, AL-59, 11kV HT cables under development
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into data center copper cables, solar cables, house wire (via distributorship), and OPGW in future; pan-India vendor approvals in Rajasthan, Mizoram, and others pending
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 15.85% due to scale and pricing power; raw material (Cu/Al) price volatility mitigated by PV clauses in government tenders; no hedging, but strong supplier relationships and inventory management
capex / expansion: H1FY26 capex: Rs. 16.45 Cr. (land, building, machinery); H2FY26: Rs. 6-7 Cr. for cable division; total capex to reach Rs. 160-170 Cr. by FY27-28 to support Rs. 1,000 Cr. order book target
capital allocation: IPO proceeds (Rs. 96 Cr.) used for Dankuni facility acquisition and machinery; future capex funded by internal accruals and potential debt/equity infusion for EPC execution; no dividend policy mentioned
risks & watch-items: EPC competition from KEC, Polycab, Calcutta-based players; execution risk in new Dankuni ramp-up; working capital pressure from EPC projects; raw material price spikes beyond PV clause coverage; delayed government payments (minor, 10-20 days)
management quality / tone: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; clear roadmap for capacity doubling, EPC entry, and pan-India expansion; transparent on capex needs and funding strategy; emphasis on operational discipline and market share capture
non-obvious takeaways: EPC division led by ex-30-year veteran Rajesh Jhunjhunwala signals serious intent; vendor approvals in Punjab/Himachal are not just geographic but strategic to avoid losing bids due to lack of eligibility; Rs. 286 Cr. order book includes legacy orders, but new EPC pipeline is the real growth lever
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EPC expansion exposes JD Cables to capital-intensive, low-margin competition | Laser Cables | loser | Medium | Smaller regional EPC player with limited capacity; JD's vertical integration and IPO-funded scale will erode its tender competitiveness |
| Rising demand for transmission-distribution cables from RDSS and grid projects | Power Grid Corporation of India | beneficiary | High | JD Cables' vendor approvals and capacity expansion directly enable it to capture more RDSS-related cable supply contracts |

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.
